$comment: Deterministic secret-scrubbing rules for tracer-bullet fixtures. Each rule redacts a known secret SHAPE to a stable placeholder so fixtures stay diff-stable and shape-preserving. This is the auditable source of truth referenced by SCRUBBING.md. Order matters: earlier rules win on overlapping matches. Never relax a rule without a manual re-review of every fixture.

detectRules.$comment: VERIFICATION-ONLY rules, used by verify.mjs — never by scrub.mjs. They exist to be an INDEPENDENT cross-check on the redactor, so they are deliberately LOOSER (lower quantifiers) than `rules` above: if someone ever tightens a scrub quantifier past a real secret, the detector still catches the residue and the gate fails. They are NOT a hand-copy of `rules` (that drift is exactly the bug SCRUBBING.md:59-65 shipped), and they are NOT a projection of them (that would be a tautology that tests nothing). Two hard constraints: (a) zero hits on this repo's own vocabulary — `task-break`, `task-review`, `task-shipper`, `disk-usage`, `ask-me`, `risk-score`; (b) zero hits on the placeholders `rules` emits, so scrubbed output verifies clean. Every quantifier below is above 7, the longest `sk-`-lookalike tail in (a) (`sk-shipper`).
detectRules.name: detect-anthropic-key

detectRules.$comment: OpenAI's project/service/admin keys (the default format since mid-2024) are `sk-proj-` + a ~150-char base64url payload. The hyphens and underscores in that payload break `detect-openai-key`'s `[A-Za-z0-9]` run after only 4 chars (`proj`), so neither that rule nor `rules`' `openai-api-key` sees them. This rule needs its own literal prefix rather than widening the class: `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` after a bare `sk-` would match `sk-usage-monitoring-daemon` inside `disk-usage-monitoring-daemon` — reintroducing the exact false positive this task exists to remove. NOTE: `rules` has no counterpart, so a hit here is a gate failure the operator must resolve by adding a scrub rule; see the task's follow-up list.
detectRules.name: detect-openai-project-key

detectRules.$comment: GitHub fine-grained PATs use the `github_pat_` prefix, whose third character (`i`) is outside `gh[pousr]_` — so `detect-github-token` and `rules`' `github-token` both miss them entirely. Same note as above: no `rules` counterpart yet.
detectRules.name: detect-github-fine-grained-pat

detectRules.$comment: Segments are UPPER-bounded (a real JWT header segment is tens of chars). Unbounded, `eyJ<run>` restarts a full-length scan at every `eyJ` occurrence, which is quadratic on a base64-dense 10MB tool-results file.
detectRules.name: detect-jwt

detectRules.$comment: `(?![A-Za-z0-9])` after the keyword excludes plurals, so transcript token accounting (`input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`, `apiKeySource`) does not trip the standing gate. Numeric-only values are excluded for the same reason. The name prefix is BOUNDED and preceded by a non-name character: an unbounded leading `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]*` is quadratic, and this gate scans tool-results/*.txt files up to 10MB of arbitrary command output.
detectRules.name: detect-keyish-assignment

detectRules.$comment: `example.com` is the placeholder domain the email rule emits; excluding it keeps the detector idempotent over scrubbed output. Anchored after `@` so it cannot be evaded by starting the match one character in. Local part bounded for the same anti-quadratic reason as the rule above (RFC 5321 caps it at 64 anyway).
detectRules.name: detect-email

detectRules.$comment: Each RFC-1918 detector excludes the exact range-base address the matching scrub rule collapses to.
detectRules.name: detect-private-ip-10

detectRules.$comment: Residual real home paths. `/home/USER` is the placeholder and is excluded; `/home/USERNAME` is not (no word boundary after USER), so a near-miss still fails the gate.
detectRules.name: detect-home-path

strip.$comment: JSONL-aware structural stripping, applied by scrubJsonl BEFORE the regex pass. Claude Code transcripts carry `type:"attachment"` lines whose body is the operator's installed skill/agent/MCP inventory — 63-66% of transcript bytes and a pure environment-config leak with no fixture value. The line is kept (count, ordering, and the uuid/parentUuid chain must survive so Phase-3's tailer still has something to walk); only the `attachment` body is replaced by `{type:<kind>,stripped:true}`. `attachmentTypes` is the observed-kinds inventory and is what gets stripped when `stripAllAttachments` is false; with it true, every attachment kind is stripped (fail-closed against kinds a future Claude Code release adds).
strip.$systemHookComment: Task 1.7 Open Question 3, resolved 2026-08-02 and implemented 2026-08-05. `type:"system"` / `subtype:"stop_hook_summary"` lines carry `hookInfos[].command` — the operator's OTHER registered hook commands, verbatim (observed: a $SUPERSET_HOME_DIR/hooks/notify.sh invocation). That is operator environment config, the same class the attachment strip exists to remove, and no regex rule can reach it: the values are ordinary shell text with no secret SHAPE, so `detectRules` scores them clean and verify.mjs exits 0 — which is exactly why this survived four captures. Present in ALL FOUR sets (compaction 10, multi-turn 6, large-output 2, subagent 2), not only compaction. EVERY command is redacted, including agent-lens's own: a content-based allowlist would mean auditing a redactor by reading the strings it chose to keep, and the fixture proves agent-lens ran from its envelopes, not from this field. The line, the array length, `hookCount` and each entry's `durationMs` all survive, so shape and ordering are preserved for the tailer.
strip.$exemptComment: `compact_boundary` is the compaction experiment's entire payload (Q4: compactMetadata + logicalParentUuid + isCompactSummary + the two-root parentUuid forest), so it is never touched. It carries no `hookInfos` today, which makes this belt-and-braces — it exists so a future Claude Code release that adds hook fields to the boundary record cannot silently gut the one set that exists to study it.

anonymize.$comment: Path/identity anonymization applied AFTER regex redaction. Set homeDir/username at runtime via --home and --user flags; these placeholders document intent.
